title: 1965 AHSME Problem 38
statement: \(A\) takes \(m\) times as long to do a piece of work as \(B\) and \(C\) together; \(B\) takes \(n\) times as long as \(C\) and \(A\) together; and \(C\) takes \(x\) times as long as \(A\) and \(B\) together. Then \(x,\) in terms of \(m\) and \(n,\) is:

solutions.text:
Let the work rates be \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c.\) The time statements give \[ \begin{gathered} b+c=ma,\\ c+a=nb,\\ a+b=xc. \end{gathered} \] From the first two, \[ \frac ba=\frac{m+1}{n+1}\] and \[\frac ca=\frac{mn-1}{n+1}.\] Hence \[ x=\frac{a+b}{c} =\frac{m+n+2}{mn-1}. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let the work rates of \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) be \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\)
Translate the first two conditions as \(b+c=ma\) and \(c+a=nb\)
